newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine broker to buy more shares in tractor firm.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine broker to buy more shares in tractor firm.

text.p: A Ukrainian brokerage firm which bought 7,000 shares in the VAT Kharkivsky Traktorny Zavod (KTZ) plans to increase its stake in the country's biggest tractor plant, a broker said on Thursday.
"We will buy more," Kiril Artamonov of IK Vointer told Reuters. "It's a company that's in good shape."
The State Property Fund, the privatisation agency, offered 12 percent of shares in the eastern plant, which employs 15,000 people, on the Ukrainian Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
Almost all of them were sold at 0.25-0.30 hryvnia, with a second buyer, Kharkiv's SVS brokerage, purchasing 23,000 shares.
The total purchase price was 4,350,070 hryvnias ($2,326,240).
The tractor maker is one of 208 enterprises which the Fund is putting up for strategic investment, but it has not said what percentage of shares will be put up for tender.
The privatisation agency announced last month that it planned to sell 19 percent of the company on the stock exchange, and did not explain why it sold a smaller amount.
KTS's charter capital has been valued at 4,350,000 hryvnias.
